clauses.reason: The title and enacting words of EO 10656 recite that the President acted as President of the United States to further the availability of intelligence of the highest order; they operate through the sections that follow. It ended when EO 10938 of May 4, 1961 revoked the order: Sec. 4 of that order states, in the held Federal Register text, "is hereby revoked." directly after the number and date of EO 10656. No earlier end is shown: the only instrument in the chain for this order is EO 10938, and the held texts that cite the number are the text files of EO 10938 and EO 10939, the latter containing the same sentence only because it shares the Federal Register page.

Section 1 of EO 10656 establishes the President's Board of Consultants on Foreign Intelligence Activities, provides that its members are appointed by the President from outside the Government and serve without compensation but may receive transportation and per-diem allowances. The Board and its membership rule continued while the order was in force. It ended when EO 10938 of May 4, 1961 revoked the order: Sec. 4 of that order states, in the held Federal Register text, "is hereby revoked." directly after the number and date of EO 10656. No earlier end is shown: the only instrument in the chain for this order is EO 10938, and the held texts that cite the number are the text files of EO 10938 and EO 10939, the latter containing the same sentence only because it shares the Federal Register page.

Section 2 directs the Board to review the foreign intelligence activities of the Government and the performance of the Central Intelligence Agency and to report its findings to the President semi-annually or more often; the semi-annual report is a recurring duty, not a single deadline. It ended when EO 10938 of May 4, 1961 revoked the order: Sec. 4 of that order states, in the held Federal Register text, "is hereby revoked." directly after the number and date of EO 10656. No earlier end is shown: the only instrument in the chain for this order is EO 10938, and the held texts that cite the number are the text files of EO 10938 and EO 10939, the latter containing the same sentence only because it shares the Federal Register page.

Section 3 directs the Board and its members to consult with the Director of Central Intelligence and other intelligence elements and authorizes the Director and those elements to make information available to the Board. It was a continuing provision. It ended when EO 10938 of May 4, 1961 revoked the order: Sec. 4 of that order states, in the held Federal Register text, "is hereby revoked." directly after the number and date of EO 10656. No earlier end is shown: the only instrument in the chain for this order is EO 10938, and the held texts that cite the number are the text files of EO 10938 and EO 10939, the latter containing the same sentence only because it shares the Federal Register page.

Section 4 requires each Board member to execute an undertaking not to reveal classified information obtained through service on the Board except to the President or persons he designates. The undertaking requirement operated while members served under the order. It ended when EO 10938 of May 4, 1961 revoked the order: Sec. 4 of that order states, in the held Federal Register text, "is hereby revoked." directly after the number and date of EO 10656. No earlier end is shown: the only instrument in the chain for this order is EO 10938, and the held texts that cite the number are the text files of EO 10938 and EO 10939, the latter containing the same sentence only because it shares the Federal Register page.

Section 5 provides that the allowances in section 1 and other expenditures of the Board are paid from the "Special Projects" appropriation in Title I of the General Government Matters Appropriation Act, 1956. It was a funding provision tied to the Board's activities. It ended when EO 10938 of May 4, 1961 revoked the order: Sec. 4 of that order states, in the held Federal Register text, "is hereby revoked." directly after the number and date of EO 10656. No earlier end is shown: the only instrument in the chain for this order is EO 10938, and the held texts that cite the number are the text files of EO 10938 and EO 10939, the latter containing the same sentence only because it shares the Federal Register page.

Section 6 states that the order is effective as of January 13, 1956, which fixed the date from which the order operated and ended with the order. It ended when EO 10938 of May 4, 1961 revoked the order: Sec. 4 of that order states, in the held Federal Register text, "is hereby revoked." directly after the number and date of EO 10656. No earlier end is shown: the only instrument in the chain for this order is EO 10938, and the held texts that cite the number are the text files of EO 10938 and EO 10939, the latter containing the same sentence only because it shares the Federal Register page.

research_rationale:
EO 10656 (1956-02-06; Establishing the President's Board of Consultants on Foreign Intelligence Activities) was read in full from the held Federal Register text (21 FR 859). Its own terms contain no end date or end condition; section 6 only sets an effective date of January 13, 1956. It ended on 1961-05-04 by express revocation in EO 10938 Sec. 4 (26 FR 3951), which in the same order established the President's Foreign Intelligence Advisory Board as a new body; the later order does not transfer the old Board's members or commands, so it is not treated as a savings transfer. The machine inventory omitted section 1 and section 6 and is replaced by seven scopes.
